tasks.short: Prepare the shift briefing, brief officers on current operations, explain operations one to one during the shift and answer officers' questions.

steps.what: Police sergeant prepares the briefing from incidents, wanted persons and points of attention
Police sergeant explains police operations to subordinates in the shift briefing
Police sergeant explains operations one to one during the shift
Police sergeant answers officers' questions by message

tasks.design: A briefing page in the police information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) fills itself with the last shift's incidents, open wanted notices and points of attention for the area, and the sergeant adds context. Briefing, explaining and answering questions stay with the sergeant; the page holds no risk scores of people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefings were assembled by searching several screens and copying items.
tasks.enabler_now: Police information systems can fill briefing pages from incident records.
tasks.still_hard: What matters for this shift is the sergeant's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a quiet street needs attention tonight.

reach.learn: Whether shared briefing pages improve area knowledge.

evidence.claim: Police information systems can fill briefing pages from incident records.
Crime-risk prediction based solely on profiling is banned.

assumptions: Boundary: from incident records to answered questions; operational orders are outside.
Input contract: incidents recorded by officers; wanted notices from the national systems; fallback is searching screens.
Briefing and explaining do not change.

incremental.description: Police sergeant checks the briefing page before each shift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is explaining in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep the shift log, review officers' incident reports, write the end-of-shift report, return reports for correction and check records are filed and kept by the rules.

steps.what: Police sergeant maintains logs of shift events and deployments
Police sergeant reviews officers' incident reports for completeness
Police sergeant prepares the end-of-shift report
Police sergeant e-mails reports back to officers for correction
Police sergeant directs the handling and maintenance of departmental records

tasks.design: The shift log fills from dispatch events and unit status in the police information system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and required-field checks flag gaps in incident reports for the sergeant to review. The end-of-shift report is a template with counts and the incidents the sergeant marks. Reports needing correction go back to the officer inside the system, and a records view shows what is unfiled or due for deletion. No narrative is generated, since reviewing drafts has not saved time in a police trial.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs and shift reports were typed from notes, and corrections went by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Police systems can fill logs from dispatch data and check required fields.
tasks.still_hard: Report quality depends on what officers write.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which incident needs a fuller report for the prosecutor.
tasks.altitude: The sergeant reviews flagged gaps instead of reading every field.

reach.learn: Whether field checks cut returned reports.

evidence.claim: Anchorage police ended a three-month trial of AI-drafted reports because reviewing drafts ate the time saved; an independent study found no real time saving.
No adverse decision may rest solely on automated processing of police data without prior human intervention.

assumptions: Boundary: from dispatch events to records in order; prosecution files are outside.
Input contract: dispatch events from the control room; report fields set by the national police; fallback is typing from notes.
Officers' correction time is outside the sergeant's savings.

already_counted.description: Police sergeant reviews flagged report gaps.
Police sergeant marks incidents for the shift report.

incremental.description: Police sergeant corrects log entries from wrong dispatch codes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Review still needs the sergeant's reading.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read new instructions and legal changes, write a short summary, send it to the team, explain changes in the briefing and answer questions about the new rules.

steps.what: Police sergeant reads new instructions and amended laws
Police sergeant writes a short summary of the implications for the team

loop.input: The new instruction or legal text and the team's tasks; no case data.
loop.output: A short summary of what changes for the team, each point citing the paragraph it rests on.
loop.check: Code rejects points without a cited paragraph; the sergeant edits and approves the summary.
loop.stop: Approved by the sergeant, or after two redrafts the sergeant writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legal texts need rewording for daily practice; a template cannot do that.

steps.what: Police sergeant e-mails the summary to the team
Police sergeant informs personnel of changes in regulations and policies in the briefing
Police sergeant answers officers' questions about the new rules

loop.input: An officer's question and the current rule texts and instructions.
loop.output: An answer quoting the paragraph it rests on, or a hand-off to the sergeant.
loop.check: Code shows only answers with a quoted paragraph from the current texts; anything else goes to the sergeant; officers are told the answer comes from a tool.
loop.stop: One answer per question; follow-ups and unclear cases go to the sergeant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Officers ask in their own words; a keyword search returns too much.

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts a short summary of what a new instruction or law means for the team, citing paragraphs, and the sergeant edits and approves it before it goes out from the document space ({DOCS}). An answer desk on the current rule texts answers routine questions with the quoted paragraph and hands the rest to the sergeant. Reading the changes and explaining them in the briefing stay with the sergeant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Summaries were written by hand, and the same questions came in again and again.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise and answer from given texts with citations.
tasks.still_hard: How a rule applies on the street is a judgement call.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining what a new rule means in a tense situation.
tasks.altitude: The sergeant edits summaries and answers only the harder questions.

reach.learn: Whether officers use the answer desk on duty.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise and answer from given texts with quoted sources.
Annex III lists law enforcement uses and worker management as high-risk from 2 December 2027; explaining rules to staff is neither.

assumptions: Boundary: from rule changes to answered questions; writing policy is outside.
Input contract: rule texts and instructions from police headquarters; fallback is the sergeant answering everything.
Reading and explaining do not change.
No case data go into the tools.
research_questions: How many questions does the answer desk resolve?

incremental.description: Police sergeant reports outdated rule texts to headquarters.

approvals.approved_version: The summary as edited and approved by the sergeant in s2; changes need a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Reading and explaining stay with the sergeant.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan training on procedures, train officers in practice scenarios, coach them after incidents and record who completed which training.

steps.what: Police sergeant plans training on procedures for the team
Police sergeant trains staff in proper police work procedures with practice scenarios
Police sergeant coaches officers on the job after incidents
Police sergeant tracks who completed which training in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Training sessions are planned in the learning system ({LMS}), which records attendance and completed modules per officer, so no spreadsheet is kept. Training in scenarios and coaching after incidents stay with the sergeant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training was tracked in a spreadsheet per team.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems record attendance and completions.
tasks.still_hard: Shift work makes it hard to get everyone to training.
tasks.human_edge: Debriefing a hard arrest so the officer learns without losing confidence.

reach.learn: Whether completion data show gaps earlier.

evidence.claim: Learning systems record training attendance and completions per person.
Systems able to monitor staff performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from training needs to training records; certification exams are outside.
Input contract: training needs set by the team chief; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Training and coaching do not change.
Officers' training time is outside the sergeant's savings.
research_questions: Do mandatory training gaps close sooner?

incremental.description: Police sergeant checks attendance lists in the system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is training and coaching in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The police sergeant keeps briefing, coaching, judgement on reports and explaining rules; assembling briefings, typing logs and repeat questions shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A sergeant who spends saved hours on the street with the team.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
